title: Pre-registration: three conversions and three shard-0 scores (S16-V sub-4-bit flip, alt-calibration hydrated, K6-parity)
why_this_file_exists: all three conversions are prediction tests. This file records the exact recipe, the exact command, the predicted bytes, the predicted KLD with its derivation and the decision rule for each of them, and is committed and pushed BEFORE any of the three conversion commands is executed. The commit that adds this file is the registration; the conversion logs carry UTC timestamps that are strictly later.

surrogate_method.what: second, independent estimator for conditions 1 and 3: exllamav3's own per-module Hessian-weighted relative proxy error, laddered at K3..K8 in receipts/error-driven-ladder.json, weighted by sqrt(out_energy) and scaled by the implied scale the published calibration fitted on a uniform role-group move

self_check.what: recomputing the published mlp_to_K4 sqrt_energy objective delta from the ladder with this script's own code

surrogate_method.published_verdict_on_the_surrogate: No rule is calibrated. The rule the plan selected, `rel`, changes the sign of its implied scale across the four pairs and predicts -0.000251 for the reallocation against a measured +0.000366 — which is exactly why the error-driven build lost. `numel` also gets that sign wrong. `abs` and `sqrt_energy` get the sign right on all four pairs, but out of sample they are off by up to 4.4x and 2.5x respec

conditions.name: S16-V sub-4-bit flip
conditions.why: docs/34 §6 and receipts/vram-class-verdict.json rest the 16 GB NO-GO on an ABSENCE: no width below 4 bits has ever been measured for KLD in this family, at any role, on any suite. docs/34's flip list item (1) is exactly this measurement -- one conversion, one shard, no 16 GB card needed -- and calls it the blocking item.

exact_environment.why_the_override_names_the_body: EXL3_BITS_OVERRIDE is matched against every key in f_targets and the MTP draft layer's three MLP projections are among them, so the loose '^.*mlp\.' form the hydrated build used would carry them to K3 too. docs/34 6.1 specifies mtp_draft all K4 for S16-V and 6.2's 212,636,704 B mtp_draft row is the all-K4 figure, so the loose form would land 33,423,360 B below the published byte prediction for a recipe reason rather than a byte-law reason. MTP width cannot reach the KLD: the fidelity protocol never engages MTP.

predicted_bytes.source: docs/34 §6.2, byte law summed over roles; disk = payload + 24.0 MB
predicted_bytes.label: prediction

point_estimate_byte_law.derivation: hydrated quantized-weight bytes 18121386596 - S16-V quantized-weight bytes 10245925476 = 7875461120 fewer bytes over ~25.6B quantized weights = -2.461 bpw; the 3.73x-per-bit constant gives 25.5x more KLD, so 0.002700 x 25.5 = 0.0689
point_estimate_byte_law.caveats: the uniform-bpw form assumes error is spread in proportion to bytes; S16-V moves five role groups at once, three of them by three bits, and the 3.73x constant is measured only over K3..K8 rungs of a proxy error, never against KLD below 4 bits. Extrapolation, not an estimate.

point_estimate_surrogate.derivation: sqrt_energy objective (w_m = sqrt(out_energy)) over the 400 laddered body modules: hydrated 4.8230, S16-V 105.4, delta 100.6. Scaled by the two implied scales the published surrogate calibration fitted on its two UNIFORM role-group pairs (0.000289 from attention K6->K5, 0.000555 from MLP->K4) this gives 0.0318 to 0.0585.
point_estimate_surrogate.extrapolated_rungs: 96 of 400 body modules have no measured K3 rung (numel below the 52M big-module threshold, so their ladder starts at K4); their K3 proxy error is extrapolated by continuing the module's own K5->K4 ratio one further bit.
point_estimate_surrogate.caveat: the published calibration verdict is that NO rule is calibrated: sqrt_energy is merely the only sign-correct rule with a bounded scale spread (2.51x, worst out-of-sample ratio 2.47x). Treat this bracket as an order-of-magnitude check on docs/34 §6.4's range, which it corroborates.

predicted_mean_kld.registered_falsification: the registered range is 0.03-0.10. A measured mean below 0.02 or above 0.20 falsifies both estimators and the design study's fidelity paragraph has to be rewritten.

conditions.acceptance_question: does sub-4-bit fidelity justify a 16 GB SKU?

registered_decision_rule.YES: measured shard-0 token_mean_kld <= K4's 0.010345 -- sub-4-bit costs no more than the worst ALREADY PUBLISHED candidate. Flip item (1) passes outright; the 16 GB no-go would then rest only on items (2)-(4) and the fidelity argument is withdrawn.
registered_decision_rule.BORDERLINE: measured mean in (0.010345, 0.030] -- worse than every published candidate but below docs/34 §6.4's predicted range. Item (1) is answered with a number that a card may print; the SKU verdict stays NO-GO on the arithmetic and the remaining items, and the checkpoint is preserved as a research repo.
registered_decision_rule.NO: measured mean > 0.030, i.e. inside or above the predicted range. Sub-4-bit fidelity does not justify a 16 GB SKU; docs/34 §6 stands as a design study with item (1) now measured rather than absent.
registered_decision_rule.tail_side_condition: reported alongside, not part of the rule: docs/34 calls K4's p99.9 of 0.5555 (10M suite) already the worst of the five published candidates. The shard-0 p99.9 and max of S16-V are reported in every case.

conditions.preservation_policy: clear NO -> receipt records the recompute cost and the checkpoint is deleted; BORDERLINE or YES -> uploaded as a research repo like the error-driven one, and Main is told.

conditions.name: alt-calibration hydrated rebuild
conditions.why: docs/37 settled ALLOCATION at a fixed byte budget and left CONTENT untested. This is the last zero-byte fidelity lever: identical widths, identical byte sizes, a deliberately different calibration corpus.
conditions.recipe: the published hydrated recipe, unchanged: MLP gate/up K5, down K6, attention K6 serialized (calibrated), lm_head K6/mcg, quantized MTP, BF16 embed+vision

the_one_change.what: exllamav3/conversion/standard_cal_data -- the six .utf8 files the converter's own get_default_calibration reads -- replaced by same-byte-size samples drawn from a disjoint public source

default_corpus.what: exllamav3's shipped standard calibration data: c4, code, multilingual, technical, tiny, wiki

alt_corpus.what: Project Gutenberg literary prose, 13 complete public-domain books, cut to the SAME byte size as each default file and formatted for the same reader (wiki.utf8 as <doc> articles, tiny.utf8 as <|endoftext|>-separated chunks, c4/multilingual as paragraph-per-line, code/technical as raw sequential text)
alt_corpus.disjointness: 19th-century literary prose only. No web text, no source code, no technical documentation, no encyclopaedia text; the multilingual file is French/German/Spanish/Italian literary prose rather than the shipped mix. Deliberately the worst realistic domain mismatch that is still natural language.

the_one_change.row_pipeline_unchanged: 250 rows x 2048 tokens (211 text rows + 39 seeded random rows), the same reader functions, the same weights

predicted_bytes.expectation: byte SIZES identical to the published hydrated build file for file, tensor bytes different. EXL3 K5/K6 module sizes are fixed by width and shape, so no size can move; only the packed values can.
predicted_bytes.control: the sibling rebuild with the DEFAULT corpus already differed in the tensor bytes of 3 of 16 files at identical sizes (/var/tmp/work/kld8/sibling-bytes.json, receipts/converter-determinism.json)

predicted_mean_kld.derivation: no law predicts this one -- there is no calibration-content term in any model this project has fitted, which is the reason the experiment exists. The registered prediction is reasoned: exllamav3 accumulates its Hessian over 512,000 calibration tokens, and the quantization error at K5/K6 is dominated by weight geometry rather than by which natural text drove the activations, so the effect should be SMALL; but the alt corpus is a deliberate domain mismatch against a suite that is not 19th-century literature, so it should be non-zero and POSITIVE. Registered: +1e-05 to +2e-04 on a hydrated base of 0.002700, i.e. between the 3.76e-06 converter-draw noise floor and a quarter of the 0.000710 one-bit attention move. Registered point 0.00275 (hydrated + 5e-05).

conditions.acceptance_question: does calibration CONTENT matter at these widths, at zero byte cost?

registered_decision_rule.content_does_not_matter: the paired 95% CI of (alt - published) contains zero AND |difference| <= 2.9e-05, the half-width of the same-corpus sibling-rebuild control (paired -3.755e-06 [-2.854e-05, +2.062e-05]). Then converter-draw noise bounds the whole content effect and the lever is closed at this width.
registered_decision_rule.content_matters: the paired 95% CI excludes zero. The magnitude is then reported as a fraction of the smallest published margin this project draws conclusions from (hydrated vs error-driven, 0.000366) and of a one-bit move (hydrated vs context, attention K6->K5, 0.000710).
registered_decision_rule.either_way: publishable. docs/37's framing applies: allocation solved, content tested.

conditions.preservation_policy: the checkpoint is a same-bytes sibling of a published artifact and carries no release value; recompute cost recorded, deleted after scoring unless the effect is large enough to want the artifact.

conditions.name: K6-parity
conditions.why: docs/29 L189-198: the Q6_K loss is a byte gap, not an engineering gap, and that is testable. Q6_K spends +1.183 GiB over hydrated's payload across ~25.6B quantized weights = +0.397 bpw; the 3.73x-per-bit constant predicts a 1.69x KLD advantage for that spend against an observed 1.77x net-of-floor, i.e. Q6_K sits ON our own scaling curve. The parity build asks whether our recipe matches or beats Q6_K at equal bytes.
conditions.recipe: the published hydrated recipe with exactly ONE change: MLP gate_proj and up_proj promoted K5 -> K6. down stays K6, attention K6 serialized, lm_head K6/mcg, MTP as hydrated, BF16 embed+vision.
conditions.prediction_class: uniform role-group promotion -- the class the EDA surrogate calibration found sign-correct, unlike the between-role reallocation at a fixed budget that it failed (receipts/error-driven-surrogate-calibration.json)

predicted_bytes.derivation: hydrated payload 21586964548 + 2 x 713031680 (gate and up, 64 modules each, K5->K6 costs exactly the byte difference between the published K5 gate role and the published K6 down role) + 22282240 (the MTP layer's gate and up, which the override regex also matches, at 1 bit per parameter) = 23035310148
predicted_bytes.label: prediction

predicted_mean_kld.registered_headline_source: docs/29 L195, the figure already on the record

byte_law_at_q6k_surplus.derivation: hydrated 0.002700 / 3.73^0.397 = 0.001601. This is docs/29's ~0.0016: it charges the parity build Q6_K's byte surplus rather than its own.

byte_law_at_own_spend.derivation: the parity build spends 1448345600 bytes = 1.349 GiB over hydrated, which over ~25.6B quantized weights is +0.4526 bpw; 3.73^0.4526 = 1.815x, so 0.002700 / 1.815 = 0.001488
byte_law_at_own_spend.note: the parity build buys MORE bytes than Q6_K's surplus (1.349 GiB against 1.183), so its own-spend prediction sits below docs/29's headline.

role_share_bound.derivation: gate+up carry 77.1% of the sqrt-energy-weighted proxy error at hydrated widths; promoting them one bit divides that share by the measured MLP K5->K6 rung ratio 3.7390 (docs/37 §3.1), leaving a factor (1-0.7711)+0.7711/3.7390 = 0.4352, so 0.002700 x 0.4352 = 0.001175
role_share_bound.caveat: assumes the whole KLD scales with the weighted proxy error and that the un-promoted roles contribute no floor of their own. This is the most aggressive of the three and is registered as the lower end.

surrogate_scaled.derivation: sqrt_energy objective delta for gate/up K5->K6 is -2.7243; scaled by the two uniform role-group scales (0.000555, 0.000289) that is -0.001511 to -0.000788 on the hydrated mean.

predicted_mean_kld.registered_consequence: every estimator predicts the parity build BEATS Q6_K's net-of-floor 0.001528 or matches it. The sharp pre-registered claim is therefore BEATS_Q6K or MATCHES_Q6K; MISSES falsifies the byte decomposition.

conditions.acceptance_question: does the parity build land WITHIN [Q6_K net 0.001528, Q6_K measured 0.002035], or BEAT it (below the net figure)?

registered_decision_rule.BEATS_Q6K: measured mean < 0.001528 (Q6_K's net-of-floor estimate). Our recipe is better than GGUF Q6_K at equal bytes; the 6-bit-class loss in receipts/cross-engine-comparator.json was a byte gap and is now closed. Release candidate for a fifth repo.
registered_decision_rule.MATCHES_Q6K: measured mean in [0.001528, 0.002035], i.e. between Q6_K net and Q6_K measured. Indistinguishable from Q6_K at equal bytes once the cross-engine floor's own slack is admitted; still a release candidate.
registered_decision_rule.MISSES: measured mean > 0.002035 (Q6_K's measured upper bound). Q6_K is better than our recipe at equal bytes and the loss is NOT purely a byte gap; the byte-law prediction is falsified in magnitude and docs/29's decomposition must be rewritten.
registered_decision_rule.owner_override_on_preservation: the checkpoint is KEPT AND UPLOADED whatever the result -- owner priority, stated at scope-addition time.

pairings: published hydrated (report-hyd.json, mean 0.002700) -- same engine, same reference capture, no cross-engine term

GGUF Q6_K (receipts/gguf-report-q6_k.json, mean 0.002035) -- SAME 512 contexts and the same suite token, but the candidate was captured in llama.cpp, so this pairing carries the cross-engine term measured at 0.000507 mean (receipts/gguf-report-engine-floor.json). A GGUF number is an upper bound on its quantization error; the net figure is the naive subtraction and KL is not additive, so the net column is an estimate, not an identity.
conditions.preservation_policy: keep and upload the checkpoint in every branch of the decision rule.

addenda.when: before any of the three conversions ran
addenda.what: condition 3's byte-parity claim is qualified: 'equal bytes' on the file is NOT equal bytes on the transformer body, because GGUF Q6_K quantizes its token embedding and our builds serialize the embedding at BF16
addenda.evidence: receipts/gguf-q6_k-tensor-accounting.json, produced by tools/gguf_tensor_table.py from the GGUF's own tensor table read over an HTTP range request (the 21 GiB payload is never downloaded)

the_asymmetry.embedding: ours 2.3682 GiB against theirs 0.9713 GiB, so we spend +1.3969 GiB on the embedding at nominal parity
the_asymmetry.head: ours 0.8885 GiB against theirs 0.9713 GiB, so we spend 0.0828 GiB less on the head
the_asymmetry.body: ours 18.1963 GiB against theirs 19.3599 GiB: at a nominally LIGHTER file the GGUF's transformer body carries +1.1636 GiB MORE than ours
the_asymmetry.matmul_weights_head_plus_body: ours 19.0848 GiB against theirs 20.3312 GiB, +1.2464 GiB in their favour
the_asymmetry.axis_note: the published 21.31 GiB for Q6_K is the whole FILE; tensor sums compare as ours 21.4531 GiB against theirs 21.3025 GiB, so we are +0.1506 GiB heavier in tensors and the file figure understates our surplus by the GGUF's 10,996,704 B of metadata and padding
the_asymmetry.resident_view: with the int8 embedding overlay our embedding would be 1.184 GiB resident, narrowing the embedding asymmetry to about +0.21 GiB -- but the fidelity protocol runs NO overlay, so the scored artifact is the BF16-embedding one and the disk-form asymmetry is the one that applies to this measurement

addenda.what_this_does_to_the_acceptance_questio: nothing to the thresholds and nothing to the registered prediction, which is derived from our own byte spend and does not reference Q6_K's composition. What it qualifies is the READING: the parity build is compared against a GGUF that spends more of its equal file budget on the weights that do the matmuls. So a win for our recipe is stronger than the headline suggests, and a loss is softer -- and either way 'at equal bytes' must be written as 'at equal file bytes, with the GGUF carrying +1.1636 GiB more body because our embedding stays BF16'.
addenda.reporting_rule: this qualification is stated in the same breath as the result on the card and in the receipt, not in a footnote, and specifically alongside any claim of a win.

corpus_versus_suite_overlap.why_it_matters: the alt calibration corpus is Project Gutenberg prose, and the v5 suite's `literary` stratum is also drawn from Project Gutenberg. If any book appeared in both, the alt build would be calibrated on its own eval text and the experiment would measure leakage instead of domain mismatch.
corpus_versus_suite_overlap.checked_against: every shard-*/suite/suite-manifest.json in the v5 suite, not just the scored shard
corpus_versus_suite_overlap.conclusion: zero book overlap. Same source, same genre for one of five strata, disjoint texts.

registered_sub_prediction_per_stratum.quantity: per-stratum paired difference (alt minus published hydrated) over the same contexts, cluster-bootstrapped with the harness's own fidelity.bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, seed 1
registered_sub_prediction_per_stratum.registered_ordering: the alt corpus's disadvantage is SMALLEST on `literary` -- possibly negative, i.e. the alt build better there -- and LARGEST on `code` and `scientific`. Formally: delta(literary) < delta(code) and delta(literary) < delta(scientific).
registered_sub_prediction_per_stratum.why: the shipped corpus covers c4 web text, source code, technical prose, encyclopaedia articles and a multilingual mix, which matches 430 of the 512 contexts. The alt corpus is 19th-century literature only, which matches the 82 literary contexts and nothing else. If calibration content acts through domain match at all, it must show up in this ordering.
registered_sub_prediction_per_stratum.falsification: if `literary` is not among the two smallest deltas, the domain-match explanation is wrong even if the overall difference is significant, and whatever calibration content does at these widths is not domain matching.

addenda.predictions_changed: none. This addendum adds a check and a sub-prediction; the overall registered point, direction, interval and decision rule for condition 2 are unchanged.

addenda.when: before any of the three conversions ran; the S16-V build script had not been executed
addenda.what: condition 1's EXL3_BITS_OVERRIDE regex was narrowed from '^.*mlp\.(gate|up|down)_proj$' to the language-model body only
addenda.why: the loose form also matches the MTP draft layer's three MLP projections -- verified against the published hydrated build, whose MTP mlp is K5/K5/K6 from its override rather than K4 from its -mb 4 -- and docs/34 6.1 specifies mtp_draft all K4 for S16-V. The all-K4 mtp_draft row docs/34 6.2 publishes, 212,636,704 B, is re-derived to the byte here from the hydrated manifest's 283,415,584 B by charging the width deltas across the MTP module numels in receipts/error-driven-ladder.json, which confirms which recipe the published prediction assumes.
addenda.byte_effect_avoided_note: 31.9 MiB. Left in, the measured payload would have undershot the published prediction for a recipe reason and looked like a byte-law error.
addenda.fidelity_effect: none possible: the fidelity protocol never engages MTP (docs/34 7), so no MTP width can reach the measured KLD.
addenda.predictions_changed: none. Every predicted byte count, predicted mean, threshold, interval, derivation and digest in this file is byte-identical to the revision first committed; the diff is this addendum, the one regex string, its explanation, and two literal '%%' typos in prose.

order_and_disk.order: S16-V first, K6-parity second, alt-calibration third
order_and_disk.why_that_order: owner decision, recorded in addendum 3: S16-V is docs/34's blocking flip item, K6-parity tests docs/29's byte-gap decomposition on an artifact already committed to be kept and uploaded, and alt-calibration is the only one of the three whose result cannot move a published verdict -- the hydrated recipe, its bytes and its number stay exactly as published whichever way it lands.
order_and_disk.disk_discipline: each conversion's working directory is deleted immediately after its convert step (nothing downstream reads it), each candidate's hidden capture is deleted after its replay, and df is checked between conversions. /var/tmp/work/kld9/hidden/hidden-{ctx,fp8,hyd,k4,nvfp4} belongs to RentalFidelityBatch2 and is not touched.
order_and_disk.if_the_window_cannot_fit_all_three: alt-calibration is the one to drop, and it is handed to ShortlistScore with this file as the plan. Its prep is fully staged and digest-proven, so it is a one-command job for whoever runs it.
